lines.text: A British engineer once studied a Tamil river dam that was already ancient.
Its name is Kallanai, the stone dam, on the Kaveri river.
Tradition credits an early Chola king, Karikala.
When? Nobody is sure. Dates range from before the common era to about the second century.
His story comes mostly from Sangam poems, and it mixes record with legend.
The idea was simple. Rough, uncut stone, laid across a sandy river bed.
Not to block the Kaveri, but to split it, and send water into the fields of the delta.
Today the structure is about three hundred and thirty metres long.
In the eighteen hundreds, British engineers repaired it and raised it.
Arthur Cotton is said to have learned from it, and the British called it the Grand Anicut.
Anicut comes from the Tamil word Anaikattu, a dam.
How much of the original stone survives under the repairs? That is not clear.
But it is often called one of the oldest water works in the world still in use.
Follow Aazhi for the next chronicle.
